questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: VF chaotic quivering no blood
questions.text: AHA Part 4 describes ventricular fibrillation. Which statement matches the manual's description?

answers.text: The ventricles beat in a slow, organized pattern
The SA node fires twice per beat causing a double-pumping effect
The atria contract too rapidly while the ventricles remain normal
The electrical activity becomes chaotic and the heart muscles quiver in a fast, unsynchronized way so the heart does not pump blood

explanations.a: Ventricular fibrillation is rapid and chaotic, not slow and organized.
explanations.b: Double-pumping is not how AHA describes VF.
explanations.c: VF affects the ventricles directly; atrial over-activity describes a different arrhythmia.
explanations.d: AHA Part 4 describes VF as chaotic electrical activity that makes the heart muscles quiver in a fast, unsynchronized way so the heart does not pump blood.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: pVT pulseless ventricular tachycardia no detectable pulse
questions.text: AHA Part 4 explains how pulseless ventricular tachycardia (pVT) becomes life-threatening. Which mechanism does the manual describe?

answers.text: The atria fibrillate while the ventricles pace normally
The heart rate becomes dangerously slow below 30 per minute
The SA node shuts down completely and the heart stops all activity
The ventricles pump so quickly and inefficiently that there is no detectable pulse

explanations.a: Atrial fibrillation with normal ventricles is a different rhythm and is not pVT.
explanations.b: pVT is a fast rhythm, not a slow one.
explanations.c: SA node shutdown describes asystole, not pVT.
explanations.d: AHA Part 4 says in extremely severe cases, the ventricles pump so quickly and inefficiently that there is no detectable pulse, which is the 'pulseless' in pVT.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: AED identifies shockable nonshockable
questions.text: According to AHA Part 4, what does the AED do after it analyzes the heart rhythm?

answers.text: It starts chest compressions automatically
It always delivers a shock regardless of the rhythm
It sends the rhythm to a physician for interpretation
It identifies the rhythm as shockable or nonshockable and advises accordingly

explanations.a: AEDs do not perform compressions; they only analyze and shock.
explanations.b: The AED only advises a shock when it identifies a shockable rhythm; it does not shock blindly.
explanations.c: AEDs analyze rhythms automatically without physician input.
explanations.d: AHA Part 4 says the AED identifies abnormal heart rhythms as shockable or nonshockable.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: ROSC signs breathing coughing palpable pulse
questions.text: A patient receives a shock from an AED and circulation appears to return. Which set of findings does AHA Part 4 cite as signs of ROSC?

answers.text: Continued absence of any pulse or movement
AED prompting 'shock advised' a second time
Breathing, coughing, or movement plus a palpable pulse or measurable blood pressure
Cyanosis and cool extremities

explanations.a: Persistent absence of pulse and movement indicates the patient remains in arrest, not ROSC.
explanations.b: Repeat 'shock advised' indicates a continuing shockable rhythm, not ROSC.
explanations.c: AHA Part 4 lists breathing, coughing, or movement and a palpable pulse or measurable blood pressure as signs of ROSC.
explanations.d: Cyanosis and cool extremities are signs of poor perfusion, not recovery.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: early defibrillation doubles triples survival
questions.text: AHA Part 4 describes the impact of early defibrillation on cardiac arrest outcomes. Which statement matches?

answers.text: Early defibrillation by lay rescuers is associated with improved survival to hospital discharge and improved 30-day and 1-year survival in adults and children
Early defibrillation only matters in hospitals, not in public settings
Survival rates are unaffected by the time to first shock
Early defibrillation has a small effect compared to other interventions

explanations.a: AHA Part 4 explicitly states early defibrillation by lay rescuers is associated with improved survival to hospital discharge and improved 30-day and 1-year survival in adults and children.
explanations.b: Public access defibrillation programs exist precisely because out-of-hospital defibrillation matters.
explanations.c: Time to first shock is one of the strongest predictors of survival from shockable arrest.
explanations.d: AHA emphasizes early defibrillation as one of the highest-impact interventions in the chain of survival.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: power on open case follow prompts step 1
questions.text: An AED arrives at the side of an adult cardiac arrest patient. What is Step 1 in AHA Part 4's universal AED operating steps?

answers.text: Power on the AED by opening the case if needed, and follow the prompts
Begin chest compressions on top of the closed AED case
Connect oxygen tubing to the AED
Type the patient's name into the AED keypad

explanations.a: AHA Part 4 Step 1 directs the operator to open the case if applicable, power on the AED — some power on automatically when the lid is opened — and follow the prompts.
explanations.b: Compressions are continued by another rescuer while the AED operator powers on the device.
explanations.c: AEDs do not connect to oxygen.
explanations.d: AEDs do not require patient identification entry to function.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: 30 seconds steps 1 and 2 power pads
questions.text: AHA Part 4 sets a specific time goal for completing the first two AED steps after the device arrives. What is that goal?

answers.text: Take at least 2 minutes to ensure proper setup
There is no time goal for the first AED steps
Spend 5 minutes preparing before turning on the device
Try to complete steps 1 and 2 within 30 seconds after the AED arrives

explanations.a: Two minutes of setup would defeat the goal of early defibrillation.
explanations.b: AHA explicitly states a 30-second target for the first two steps to minimize time to shock.
explanations.c: Five-minute preparation is far past the AHA-specified goal.
explanations.d: AHA Part 4 instructs rescuers to try to perform the first 2 steps — power on, then apply pads — within 30 seconds after the AED arrives, while a second rescuer continues CPR.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: pads bare chest peel back apply connector
questions.text: After the AED powers on, it prompts 'Apply pads to patient's bare chest.' Which AHA Part 4 actions match?

answers.text: Apply pads on top of the patient's clothing for modesty
Wait for ALS before applying any pad
Apply only one pad and leave the second wrapped
Peel the backing from the pads, apply them to the bare chest, and plug in the pads connector

explanations.a: Pads must contact bare skin; placing them over clothing prevents rhythm detection and shock delivery.
explanations.b: AEDs are designed for lay-rescuer use and do not require ALS authorization.
explanations.c: Both pads must be applied for the AED to analyze and deliver a shock.
explanations.d: AHA Part 4 Step 2 directs the operator to peel the backing from the pads, apply them to the bare chest, and plug in the pads connector if not preconnected.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: analyzing do not touch stop compressions
questions.text: When the AED prompts 'Analyzing heart rhythm. Do not touch the patient,' what does AHA Part 4 require?

answers.text: Clear the person — ensure no one is touching them, not even the rescuer giving breaths
Continue compressions to maintain perfusion during analysis
Hold the patient firmly by the shoulders
Apply oxygen by mask during the analysis

explanations.a: AHA Part 4 instructs the rescuer to clear the person for rhythm analysis, ensuring no one is touching them — not even the rescuer in charge of giving breaths.
explanations.b: Continuing compressions during analysis introduces motion artifact that prevents rhythm interpretation.
explanations.c: Holding the patient transmits motion and creates a shock hazard.
explanations.d: Oxygen near a shock creates a fire hazard and is not part of the analysis step.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: AED placed at persons side near operator
questions.text: Once the AED arrives, AHA Part 4 specifies exactly where to place it during resuscitation. Which placement is correct?

answers.text: At the foot of the patient, several feet away
At the patient's side, near the rescuer who will operate it
Across the patient's chest
Hung from a wall hook above the patient's head

explanations.a: Placing the AED at the foot makes pad application and control access cumbersome.
explanations.b: AHA Part 4 directs the operator to place the AED at the person's side near the operator, giving ready access to controls and easy pad placement while a second rescuer continues CPR from the opposite side.
explanations.c: Placing the AED on the patient's chest blocks compressions and pad placement.
explanations.d: AEDs are not used while hanging on the wall during a resuscitation.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: no shock advised resume CPR immediately
questions.text: The AED prompts 'No shock advised' after analyzing the rhythm of an adult patient. According to AHA Part 4, what should the team do next?

answers.text: Stop CPR and wait for the next analysis
Disconnect the pads to reset the device
Place the patient in the recovery position
Immediately resume high-quality CPR starting with chest compressions

explanations.a: Stopping CPR after a no-shock prompt abandons the most effective intervention available between rhythm checks.
explanations.b: Disconnecting pads is unnecessary and would prevent the next analysis.
explanations.c: Recovery position is for someone with normal breathing, not an ongoing arrest.
explanations.d: AHA Part 4 directs immediate resumption of high-quality CPR, starting with chest compressions, after either a shock or a 'no shock advised' prompt.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: anterolateral right upper clavicle left lateral midaxillary
questions.text: An instructor demonstrates anterolateral AED pad placement. Which positions match the AHA Part 4 description?

answers.text: One pad vertically on the right upper chest just under the clavicle; one horizontally on the left lateral ribs below the axilla at the midaxillary line
One pad on the abdomen and the other on the upper back
Both pads on the upper sternum side by side
One pad on the right thigh and the other on the left arm

explanations.a: AHA Part 4 anterolateral placement places one pad vertically on the right upper chest just under the clavicle and the other horizontally on the left lateral ribs, with the middle of the pad below the axilla at the midaxillary line.
explanations.b: Abdomen and upper back are not the AHA-described anterolateral landmarks.
explanations.c: Two pads on the upper sternum side by side would not span the heart.
explanations.d: Limb placement does not direct current through the heart.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: AP anterior center chest posterior center back
questions.text: AHA Part 4 describes anteroposterior (AP) pad placement as an option. Which of the two AP configurations does the manual list?

answers.text: One pad in the center of the bare chest (anterior) and the other in the center of the back (posterior)
Both pads stacked on the lateral chest wall
One pad on the forehead and one on the abdomen
Both pads on the same arm, one on each side

explanations.a: AHA Part 4 lists AP placement as one pad in the center of the bare chest (anterior) and the other in the center of the back (posterior) as one of the two AP options.
explanations.b: Stacking pads on the lateral wall does not direct shock energy across the heart.
explanations.c: Forehead and abdomen are not AED pad positions.
explanations.d: Both pads on a single limb cannot deliver a shock through the heart.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: AP alternate left chest sternum nipple left back spine
questions.text: AHA Part 4 describes a second AP placement option with both pads on the left side of the body. Which landmarks does the manual specify?

answers.text: One pad on the right shoulder blade, the other on the right hip
One pad on the left chest between the left side of the sternum and the left nipple; the other on the left back next to the spine
One pad on the abdomen, the other above the right ear
One pad on the left foot, the other on the right hand

explanations.a: Shoulder-and-hip placement is not described in AED pad-placement guidance.
explanations.b: AHA Part 4 describes the alternate AP option as one pad on the left side of the chest between the left side of the sternum and the left nipple, with the other pad on the left side of the back next to the spine.
explanations.c: Abdomen-and-head placement is not an AED option.
explanations.d: Limb placement does not pass current through the heart.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: follow diagram on pads direct skin contact
questions.text: AHA Part 4 gives one universal instruction about pad placement that applies regardless of which configuration is used. Which statement matches?

answers.text: Always use the same configuration for every patient regardless of anatomy
Follow the placement diagram on the pads; always place pads directly on the skin
Pads can be placed over thin clothing without significant quality loss
Placement matters only if the patient has had a previous arrest

explanations.a: AP placement may be preferable in some situations such as infants or obesity; one configuration is not universally required.
explanations.b: AHA Part 4 instructs rescuers to follow the placement diagram on the pads and to always place pads directly on the skin.
explanations.c: Even thin clothing prevents proper electrode contact.
explanations.d: Correct pad placement matters for every patient and every arrest.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: pads not over clothing medication patches implanted devices
questions.text: AHA Part 4 lists three things AED pads must never be placed over. Which set matches?

answers.text: Skin, muscle, and bone
Clothing, medication patches, and implanted devices
Hair, fingernails, and sunscreen
AED pads can be placed over any surface

explanations.a: Pads are placed on bare skin, not over it.
explanations.b: AHA Part 4 explicitly states pads must not be placed over clothing, medication patches, or implanted devices.
explanations.c: Hair matters for adhesion but is not in the AHA-listed trio; sunscreen and fingernails are not restrictions.
explanations.d: AHA explicitly restricts placement over clothing, medication patches, and implanted devices.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: everybody clear loud verbal visual confirm
questions.text: Just before pressing the Shock button, AHA Part 4 directs the AED operator to perform a specific safety check. Which set of actions matches?

answers.text: Quietly count to 10 with hands on the patient
Ask each team member individually whether they are ready
Press the shock button without warning to save time
Loudly state 'Everybody clear!' and visually confirm no one is touching the patient

explanations.a: Silent counting with hands on the patient creates a safety hazard during shock delivery.
explanations.b: Polling each member individually wastes time; a single loud announcement plus visual check is the AHA technique.
explanations.c: Skipping the warning risks shocking another rescuer in contact with the patient.
explanations.d: AHA Part 4 instructs the operator to loudly state a 'clear the person' message — for example, 'Everybody clear!' — and visually confirm no one is touching the person before delivering the shock.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: shorter pre-shock pause better ROSC research
questions.text: AHA Part 4 cites research about the time between the last compression and shock delivery. Which relationship does the research show?

answers.text: The longer the gap, the higher the chance of ROSC
The gap has no measurable relationship with outcomes
A standardized 60-second gap is required for the device to charge
The shorter the gap, the better the chances of ROSC

explanations.a: Longer pre-shock pauses lower the chance of ROSC because coronary perfusion pressure drops rapidly.
explanations.b: Multiple studies establish that this gap measurably affects survival.
explanations.c: AEDs typically charge in seconds; no standardized 60-second gap is required.
explanations.d: AHA Part 4 reports that the shorter the time between the last compression and shock delivery, the better the chances of ROSC.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: compressor AED operator team coordination practice
questions.text: AHA Part 4 says minimizing the time between last compression and shock requires practice and coordination between which two team roles?

answers.text: Family liaison and documentation recorder
The Compressor and the AED operator
Hospital security and pharmacy technician
Phone caller and bystander coordinator

explanations.a: These roles do not directly affect compression-to-shock timing.
explanations.b: AHA Part 4 states the practice and coordination needed is especially between the rescuer providing compressions and the rescuer operating the AED.
explanations.c: Security and pharmacy roles are not involved in CPR-to-shock timing.
explanations.d: Phone callers and bystander coordinators are valuable but not the dyad highlighted.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: shock muscle contraction sudden jerk
questions.text: AHA Part 4 warns that when the Shock button is pressed, which physical reaction may occur in the patient?

answers.text: The patient may smile involuntarily
The patient may yawn deeply
A sudden contraction of the person's muscles
The patient will immediately stand up

explanations.a: Smiling is not a described effect of AED shock delivery.
explanations.b: Yawning is not a described effect of AED shock delivery.
explanations.c: AHA Part 4 notes the shock may produce a sudden contraction of the person's muscles.
explanations.d: A patient in cardiac arrest will not stand up when shocked.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: 5 cycles 2 min then re-analyze
questions.text: After a shock is delivered or the AED prompts 'no shock advised,' AHA Part 4 specifies a CPR duration before the AED re-analyzes. What is that duration?

answers.text: About 30 seconds of CPR
About 5 cycles or 2 minutes of high-quality CPR
About 10 minutes of CPR
No CPR — wait for ALS

explanations.a: Thirty seconds is well below the AHA-specified interval between rhythm checks.
explanations.b: AHA Part 4 specifies that after about 5 cycles or 2 minutes of high-quality CPR the AED prompts the team to re-analyze.
explanations.c: Ten minutes between checks would miss multiple opportunities to deliver indicated shocks.
explanations.d: Continuing CPR is essential; it does not depend on ALS arrival.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: hairy chest check electrodes razor sacrifice pads
questions.text: An adult cardiac arrest victim has a very hairy chest and the AED displays 'check electrodes.' Which response matches AHA Part 4 guidance?

answers.text: Continue trying to apply the same pads repeatedly until they stick
Skip pads and deliver compressions only — the AED is unusable
Use a razor to shave the area; if no razor is available and you have a second set of pads, press and quickly pull off the first set to remove hair, then apply the second set
Wet the chest hair until pads adhere

explanations.a: Re-applying pads to hair will not produce reliable contact.
explanations.b: AEDs remain usable; the issue is hair preventing electrode contact, which can be fixed.
explanations.c: AHA Part 4 says to use a razor or clippers; if no razor is available but a second set of pads is on hand, press and quickly pull the first set off to remove hair, then apply the new set.
explanations.d: Wetting the chest creates a conductive surface for shock spread and is contraindicated.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: water pull out wipe chest before pads
questions.text: A drowning victim is found in shallow water. AHA Part 4 specifies actions before AED use. Which approach is correct?

answers.text: Use the AED while the patient remains submerged
Pour additional water on the chest to ensure good conduction
Pull the person out of the water and quickly wipe the chest before attaching the pads
Wait until the patient is fully dry before any compressions

explanations.a: AEDs cannot be used safely on a person in water — water conducts electricity.
explanations.b: Adding water makes the situation worse by spreading shock energy uncontrollably.
explanations.c: AHA Part 4 directs rescuers to pull the person out of the water and quickly wipe the chest before attaching the AED pads.
explanations.d: Compressions should not be delayed for full drying; quick wiping is sufficient.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: pacemaker ICD hard lump avoid direct placement
questions.text: You see a hard lump the size of a half-deck of cards in the left upper chest of an adult patient in cardiac arrest. According to AHA Part 4, what is the correct AED action?

answers.text: Place a pad directly over the lump for stronger shock energy
Do not use the AED at all if a pacemaker or ICD is suspected
Avoid placing the AED pad directly over the implanted device, then follow the normal steps
Cut the device out before applying pads

explanations.a: Placing a pad directly over an implanted device may interfere with shock delivery and damage the device.
explanations.b: AEDs can and should be used on patients with implanted devices; the only adjustment is pad position.
explanations.c: AHA Part 4 says if you identify an implanted defibrillator or pacemaker, avoid placing the AED pad directly over the implanted device, then follow the normal steps.
explanations.d: Removing implanted devices is a surgical procedure and absolutely not part of BLS.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: medication patch remove gloves wipe before pad
questions.text: An adult patient has a nitroglycerin transdermal patch where you need to place the AED pad. Which action matches AHA Part 4?

answers.text: If it will not delay shock delivery, remove the patch with gloves and wipe the area before attaching the AED pad
Place the AED pad directly over the patch for better adhesion
Wait for ALS to remove the patch
Cut a hole in the patch and apply the pad through it

explanations.a: AHA Part 4 directs the rescuer to remove the patch with gloves and wipe the area before attaching the AED pad, provided this does not delay shock delivery.
explanations.b: Placing the pad over a patch may interfere with energy transfer and cause small burns.
explanations.c: Removing the patch is within BLS scope and should not wait for ALS.
explanations.d: Modifying the patch does not solve the energy transfer problem.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: pregnancy AED safe shock won't harm fetus
questions.text: A 30-week pregnant woman collapses in cardiac arrest. According to AHA Part 4, how should the AED be used?

answers.text: Apply pediatric pads to reduce shock energy for the fetus
Wait until after delivery before any defibrillation
Do not use an AED during pregnancy
Use the AED as you would for anyone in cardiac arrest; the shock will not harm the fetus

explanations.a: Pediatric pads deliver too low a dose for an adult and would not be effective.
explanations.b: Cardiac arrest cannot wait for delivery; immediate AED use is the correct approach.
explanations.c: Without lifesaving treatment to the pregnant person, the fetus will not likely survive.
explanations.d: AHA Part 4 says use an AED for a pregnant person in cardiac arrest as you would for anyone else; the shock will not harm the fetus.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: clothing remove undergarments jewelry stay if no contact
questions.text: An adult patient has a bulky sweater and a necklace on their chest. According to AHA Part 4, which approach is correct?

answers.text: Leave all clothing in place; AEDs work through fabric
Remove all jewelry from the entire body before AED use
Remove clothing — including undergarments covering the chest — since pads must not be over clothing; jewelry can stay unless it contacts the pads
Cut a small hole in the sweater for each pad rather than removing it

explanations.a: AED pads cannot deliver effective current through fabric.
explanations.b: Universal jewelry removal is unnecessary; only items contacting the pads matter.
explanations.c: AHA Part 4 says remove clothing — including undergarments covering the chest — because pads must not be over clothing; jewelry need not be removed unless it contacts the AED pads.
explanations.d: Cutting holes in clothing is not part of AHA technique; clothing should be moved out of the way.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: snow small puddle wipe use AED
questions.text: AHA Part 4 addresses a common question about using an AED when the patient is lying on snow or in a small puddle. What does the manual say?

answers.text: Do not use an AED if there is any water present, including snow
You may use the AED after quickly wiping the chest even if the patient is lying on snow or in a small puddle
The patient must be moved to a dry building before any AED use
Snow and puddles require a specialist to drain the area first

explanations.a: The absolute prohibition is using the AED in water; small amounts around the patient are manageable.
explanations.b: AHA Part 4 says if the person is lying on snow or in a small puddle, you may use the AED after quickly wiping the chest.
explanations.c: Moving to a dry building would cause unacceptable delays; quick wiping is the practical solution.
explanations.d: Draining the area is not a BLS step and would fatally delay care.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: child pads not for adults dose too low
questions.text: Your AED includes smaller pads designed for children younger than 8 years. AHA Part 4 explicitly cautions against one specific misuse. What is it?

answers.text: Always use child pads on adults to reduce burn risk
Child pads can be used for any patient in cardiac arrest
Do not use child pads for an adult — the shock dose is too low and will likely not be successful
Child pads expire after one use and must be discarded immediately

explanations.a: Using child pads on adults reduces shock effectiveness, not burn risk.
explanations.b: Child pads are designed only for younger pediatric use; adults need adult-dose pads.
explanations.c: AHA Part 4 explicitly states do not use child pads for an adult because they deliver a shock dose too low for an adult and will likely not be successful.
explanations.d: Child pads do not expire after a single use; the issue is dose-mismatch, not expiration.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: attenuator reduces shock two thirds
questions.text: AHA Part 7 describes how a pediatric dose attenuator works. Which statement matches the manual?

answers.text: An attenuator doubles the shock dose for small children
An attenuator eliminates the shock entirely
An attenuator is used only after ROSC is achieved
An attenuator reduces the shock dose by about two thirds

explanations.a: An attenuator reduces the shock dose; it does not double it.
explanations.b: Pediatric AED features still deliver a shock, just at a lower dose.
explanations.c: An attenuator is used during active resuscitation, not after ROSC.
explanations.d: AHA Part 7 says an attenuator reduces the shock dose by about two thirds.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: under 8 use child pads if available adult if not
questions.text: AHA Part 7 specifies AED pad selection for infants and children younger than 8. Which approach matches?

answers.text: Always use adult pads on all children regardless of size
Use child pads if available; if child pads are not available, you may use adult pads — ensure pads do not touch each other
Do not defibrillate children younger than 8 under any circumstances
Cut adult pads in half to reduce shock dose

explanations.a: Child pads are preferred for children under 8 when available.
explanations.b: AHA Part 7 says use child pads if available; if child pads are not available, you may use adult pads, ensuring the pads do not touch each other.
explanations.c: Withholding defibrillation from a child with a shockable rhythm worsens survival.
explanations.d: Cutting pads damages the electrodes and is never recommended.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: 8 to puberty adult pads do not use child
questions.text: AHA Part 7 specifies which pads to use for a child age 8 years to puberty in cardiac arrest. Which approach applies?

answers.text: Use child pads only — adult pads are too large
Skip the AED entirely until after puberty
Use adult pads — do not use child pads, which will give a dose that is likely too low
Use only home AEDs, not public-access devices

explanations.a: Child pads may deliver insufficient dose for a school-age child.
explanations.b: Skipping the AED removes a critical intervention for shockable arrest.
explanations.c: AHA Part 7 says for children 8 years to puberty, use adult pads and do not use child pads, which will likely give a shock dose that is too low.
explanations.d: AHA makes no distinction between home and public AEDs for pediatric use.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: infant manual defibrillator preferred AED second choice
questions.text: AHA Part 7 addresses defibrillation preferences for infants specifically. Which device priority does the manual state?

answers.text: A manual defibrillator is preferred; when unavailable, an AED with a pediatric dose attenuator is preferred; if neither is available, use an AED without an attenuator
An AED is always preferred over a manual defibrillator for infants
Defibrillation should not be used for infants under any circumstances
A manual defibrillator is the only acceptable device for infants

explanations.a: AHA Part 7 says for infants: a manual defibrillator is preferred; when not available, an AED with a pediatric dose attenuator is the preferred alternative; if neither is available, you may use an AED without an attenuator.
explanations.b: AHA actually prefers a manual defibrillator over an AED for infants because manual devices offer more control over energy dose.
explanations.c: Defibrillation is appropriate for infants with shockable rhythms.
explanations.d: If no manual defibrillator is available, AHA supports using an AED as described in option a.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: infant AP placement pads may overlap
questions.text: AHA Part 7 addresses pad placement for very small chests such as infants when adult pads are used. What does the manual recommend?

answers.text: Place both pads side by side on the front of the chest, allowing them to overlap
Use anteroposterior placement — one pad on the front of the chest and one on the back — to prevent the pads from touching
Place both pads on the abdomen for infants
Leave a single pad on the chest and use the device with one electrode

explanations.a: Overlapping pads create a short circuit and prevent effective shock delivery to the heart.
explanations.b: AHA Part 7 says to use AP placement — one pad on the chest and one on the back — when pads would otherwise touch each other on a very small chest.
explanations.c: Abdominal placement does not pass current through the heart.
explanations.d: AEDs require both pads to deliver a shock.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: adult dose better than no shock infant
questions.text: AHA Part 7's critical concept states a principle about using adult AED equipment on infants or children when pediatric equipment is unavailable. Which statement matches?

answers.text: Adult shock dose is always better than pediatric dose for infants
Using adult pads or adult shock dose is better than no defibrillation for an infant or child
No defibrillation is preferable to using adult pads on a child
Adult pads on an infant cause more harm than good

explanations.a: Adult dose is not always preferred; pediatric dose is preferred when available — but adult dose is better than nothing.
explanations.b: AHA Part 7's Critical Concept states: using adult pads or adult shock dose is better than no defibrillation for an infant or child.
explanations.c: Withholding defibrillation from a child with a shockable rhythm lowers survival.
explanations.d: Adult pads on an infant may deliver a higher dose than ideal but are still preferable to no shock.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: shock delivered start CPR immediately compressions
questions.text: After the AED delivers a shock and prompts 'Shock delivered. Start CPR,' what does AHA Part 4 instruct the team to do?

answers.text: Pause for 30 seconds before resuming compressions
Check the carotid pulse for 60 seconds before resuming
Discontinue CPR and wait for ALS
Immediately resume CPR starting with chest compressions

explanations.a: A 30-second pause adds an unnecessary interruption when perfusion is most needed.
explanations.b: A 60-second pulse check after a shock is contrary to AHA timing.
explanations.c: Stopping CPR prematurely abandons a critical intervention.
explanations.d: AHA Part 4 instructs the team to immediately resume CPR, starting with chest compressions, after a shock is delivered.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: continue until ALS or breathes moves reacts
questions.text: AHA Part 4 says rescuers should continue the CPR-AED cycle until two specific conditions are met. What are they?

answers.text: Until 5 cycles are completed or 10 minutes have passed
Until the AED battery dies or the family asks to stop
Until ALS professionals take over or the person begins to breathe, move, or otherwise react
Until the rescuer becomes too tired

explanations.a: There is no AHA time-out at 5 cycles or 10 minutes; care continues until ALS or response.
explanations.b: Battery death and family requests are practical issues but not the AHA-defined stopping criteria.
explanations.c: AHA Part 4 says continue until ALS professionals take over or the person begins to breathe, move, or otherwise react.
explanations.d: Rescuer fatigue is addressed by switching compressors, not by stopping care.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: pads remain attached for next reanalysis
questions.text: Once AED pads are applied, AHA Part 4 implies they should remain attached throughout the resuscitation. What purpose does this serve?

answers.text: Remove pads after each shock to allow the skin to rest
Replace the pads with a fresh set after every shock
Pads are removed only if the patient regains consciousness
Leaving pads attached allows the AED to reanalyze the rhythm after each 2-minute CPR period

explanations.a: Removing pads between shocks would prevent the AED from continuing to monitor and prompt analyses.
explanations.b: Replacing pads after every shock creates pauses and is unnecessary.
explanations.c: Pads are not removed because the patient may regain consciousness; the device continues to be used until ALS or response.
explanations.d: AHA Part 4 says after about 2 minutes of CPR the AED prompts to repeat the analyze-and-shock steps, which requires the pads to remain attached.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: CCF goal 60 percent AED use
questions.text: The high CCF goal still applies during AED use. AHA Part 5 recommends that high-performance teams target a CCF of at least what percentage?

answers.text: At least 30 percent
There is no recommended CCF target
At least 60 percent
At least 99 percent

explanations.a: 30 percent is well below the AHA-recommended target.
explanations.b: AHA does specify a CCF target precisely because higher CCF correlates with better survival.
explanations.c: AHA Part 5 recommends targeting a CCF of at least 60 percent throughout the resuscitation, including during AED use.
explanations.d: 99 percent is unrealistic given mandatory pauses for AED analysis.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: pregnant post ROSC left side uterus
questions.text: After AED-assisted resuscitation of a pregnant person achieves ROSC, AHA Part 4 gives a specific positioning recommendation. What is it?

answers.text: Place the person on their left side to improve blood flow to their heart and to the fetus
Place the person flat on their back with no positioning
Place the person face down to reduce reflux risk
Place the person sitting fully upright

explanations.a: AHA Part 4 says if the pregnant person is revived, place them on their left side to improve blood flow to their heart and therefore to the fetus.
explanations.b: Supine positioning allows the gravid uterus to compress major vessels.
explanations.c: Prone positioning blocks the airway and is contraindicated.
explanations.d: Sitting fully upright is not the AHA-recommended post-resuscitation position for a pregnant person.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: CPR do not delay high quality after shock
questions.text: AHA Part 4 has a section titled 'Do Not Delay High-Quality CPR After AED Use.' Which statement captures its core message?

answers.text: CPR can be paused indefinitely once a shock is delivered
AED use replaces the need for CPR entirely
Whether a shock is advised or not, immediately resume high-quality CPR starting with chest compressions
CPR should be started only after ALS confirms the rhythm

explanations.a: CPR must resume immediately — a shock alone rarely restores sustained circulation.
explanations.b: AED and CPR are complementary; neither replaces the other.
explanations.c: AHA Part 4 states that after either a shock or a 'no shock advised' prompt, immediately resume high-quality CPR, starting with chest compressions.
explanations.d: CPR cannot wait for ALS confirmation; it resumes immediately.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: battery pads pocket masks gloves razors scissors maintain
questions.text: AHA Part 4 lists the items someone should be designated to maintain for the AED program. Which set matches?

answers.text: Stethoscope, thermometer, tongue depressor, and bandages
IV bags, syringes, and intubation kit
Battery; adult and pediatric pads; pocket masks; gloves; razors; and scissors
Backboard, cervical collar, and traction splint

explanations.a: Diagnostic clinical instruments are not part of AED program maintenance.
explanations.b: ALS supplies are not part of an AED program maintenance list.
explanations.c: AHA Part 4 says someone should be designated to maintain the battery, adult and pediatric pads, and barrier devices such as pocket masks, gloves, razors for hairy chests, and scissors.
explanations.d: Spinal-immobilization equipment is unrelated to AED maintenance.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: cardiac emergency response plan who responds what to do
questions.text: AHA Part 4 recommends that all locations and organizations have a specific plan in place. What does it describe?

answers.text: A cardiac emergency response plan that outlines who responds and what to do in a cardiac emergency
A staff appreciation plan
A facility relocation plan
A long-term marketing plan

explanations.a: AHA Part 4 says all locations and organizations should have a cardiac emergency response plan that outlines specifically who responds and what to do during a cardiac emergency.
explanations.b: Appreciation plans do not improve outcomes from cardiac arrest.
explanations.c: Facility relocation has no bearing on cardiac emergency response.
explanations.d: Marketing plans are unrelated to AED-program effectiveness.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: PAD programs public places high risk communities
questions.text: AHA Part 4 describes Public Access Defibrillation (PAD) programs. Which statement matches the manual's description?

answers.text: PAD programs are designed to reduce time to defibrillation by placing AEDs in public places and training community members to use them
PAD programs require professional medical staff at every AED location
PAD programs are limited to hospital corridors
PAD programs are optional pilot programs with no evidence of benefit

explanations.a: AHA Part 4 says PAD programs are recommended in communities at high risk for OHCA and are designed to reduce time to defibrillation by placing AEDs in public places and training community members.
explanations.b: PAD programs specifically train laypeople, not just professional staff.
explanations.c: PAD programs target airports, convention centers, schools, offices, and other public spaces, not only hospital corridors.
explanations.d: PAD programs are supported by evidence of improved survival and are recommended by AHA.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: monitor defibrillator ALS more complex advanced rhythms
questions.text: AHA Part 4 distinguishes AEDs from monitor/defibrillators. Which statement matches the manual's description of monitor/defibrillators?

answers.text: They are simple single-button devices identical to AEDs
They have more complex features, require advanced training, and can monitor rhythms and treat more complex arrhythmias
They are only used for pediatric patients
They cannot deliver electrical shocks

explanations.a: Monitor/defibrillators are more complex than AEDs and require advanced training.
explanations.b: AHA Part 4 says ALS and other health care professionals may use monitor/defibrillators, which have more complex features, require advanced training, can monitor heart rhythms, and can treat more complex arrhythmias.
explanations.c: Monitor/defibrillators are used across all ages in clinical settings.
explanations.d: Monitor/defibrillators deliver both paced rhythms and shock therapy.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: AED mode automatic rhythm advises shock
questions.text: AHA Part 4 notes that some monitor/defibrillators can operate in a specific mode that resembles an AED. What does this mode do?

answers.text: AED mode automatically analyzes the person's heart rhythm and advises whether a shock is needed
AED mode delivers continuous pacing at 60 beats per minute
AED mode turns the device into a blood pressure monitor
AED mode is only available on pediatric-specific devices

explanations.a: AHA Part 4 says a monitor/defibrillator may be used in AED mode, which is when it automatically analyzes the person's heart rhythm and advises whether a shock is needed.
explanations.b: Continuous pacing at 60 bpm is transcutaneous pacing mode, not AED mode.
explanations.c: AED mode does not change the device to a blood pressure monitor.
explanations.d: AED mode is available on multi-function devices used for all ages.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: manufacturer instructions maintain AED properly
questions.text: AHA Part 4 specifies how AEDs should be maintained. Which approach does the manual prescribe?

answers.text: AEDs should be maintained according to the manufacturer's instructions
AEDs never need maintenance once purchased
AEDs should be stored disassembled to preserve components
AEDs should be tested during every emergency to check function

explanations.a: AHA Part 4 says AEDs should be properly maintained according to the manufacturer's instructions.
explanations.b: Batteries expire and pads degrade; regular maintenance per manufacturer instructions is required.
explanations.c: AEDs should be stored ready to use, not disassembled.
explanations.d: AEDs should be checked on a scheduled basis, not first tested during an emergency.

questions.name: AED for All Ages
questions.keyword: two rescuer CPR continues AED operator side
questions.text: AHA Part 4 explains that the AED should be placed at the patient's side near the operator specifically so another rescuer can continue CPR without interference. Which arrangement does this create?

answers.text: AED operator and Compressor on the same side with no room to work
AED at the patient's side near the operator; a second rescuer continues CPR from the opposite side without interfering with AED operation
The Compressor holds the AED while delivering compressions
The AED is placed on the patient's chest during compressions

explanations.a: The arrangement is designed to avoid crowding, not create it.
explanations.b: AHA Part 4 says placing the AED at the person's side near the operator allows a second rescuer to continue CPR from the opposite side without interfering with AED operation.
explanations.c: The Compressor's role is compressions; holding the AED is the AED operator's job.
explanations.d: Placing the AED on the patient's chest would block compressions and pad placement.
